discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where Coulomb interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and coworkers realised this system and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, controlled simply by a gate voltage. This work created the field of moiré quantum materials: a tunable platform in which Mott-like insulators, strange metals, orbital magnetism, and fractional quantum anomalous Hall states have since been observed. For the first time, the strength of electronic correlations, the band filling and the band topology can be dialled continuously in one device, turning the strongly correlated electron problem, central to condensed matter physics since Mott and Anderson, into an experimentally programmable science. Its impact on theory, experiment and computation of correlated matter is profound and lasting.
